domain: spaces for observing or caring for plants and natural environments
pool_basis: general knowledge and independent visual reasoning only

pool.scene: A botanist in a misted night-pollination glasshouse slowly folds back a vellum shade to examine a moth settled on a white flower; a recently opened petal and the moved shade connect observation to a vulnerable living moment.

Inside a narrow orchid quarantine conservatory after a shallow flood, a botanist lifts a low flowering pot onto a dry metal shelf; a water mark and newly draining roots make a small act of protection visible.

In a cloister-like fern restoration house after a roof leak, a botanist directs the last water from a soft temporary catch into a stone trough while one fragile white flowering plant stands beside the fern trays; containment and recovery share the frame.

At an alpine plant acclimation room, a botanist carefully lifts a glass humidity bell after frost recedes, inspecting the first upright white bloom; condensed drops and the cleared opening connect the prior cold enclosure to a tentative next stage.

A botanist at an indoor water-lily phenology tank lowers a slim brass measuring rail beside a newly opening pale flower at dawn; the water reflection, suspended petal and earlier closed bloom make the passage from bud to opening legible.

In a heritage citrus overwintering orangery at the end of rain, a botanist loosens a temporary dark silk support from a bent white-blossoming stem as it regains its own shape; the freed branch, damp window and slack ribbon connect care to a delicate release.
